note: Themed baskets: equal-weight groups of stocks for ideas no single ETF captures. A watchlist, not recorded ideas. Members come from IBKR's theme data (search_investment_topics / get_theme_details) and the dossier; every member is checked with IBKR (search_contracts for a US listing, get_price_snapshot avg_90d_usd_volume of at least about $20M; names in the standard universe skip the volume check). The snapshot is IBKR's change from the prior close at the time shown; after 16:00 it includes after-hours trades.

baskets.name: Texas power
baskets.story: Power generators and retailers whose growth case leans on ERCOT data-center load. A Texas data-center moratorium, which the governor's race put on the table, hits them directly; regulated utilities elsewhere (XLU) far less.
baskets.watch: Texas count and any statement from the governor-elect or PUCT on large-load interconnection; ERCOT large-load queue updates.
baskets.source: IBKR theme Data Center Power; dossier 2026-11-03

members.why: Texas-based ERCOT generator; 1.2 GW Comanche Peak colocation deal with AWS and a stated 10-15 GW ERCOT data-center load target
Houston-based; the largest ERCOT retail supplier with Texas generation
Mostly PJM nuclear, but its Freestone Texas site hosts a CyrusOne data center under a recent PUCT approval: a partial Texas name

baskets.name: Texas AI hosts
baskets.story: Former bitcoin miners converting Texas sites into AI data centers. They carry the moratorium risk on new capacity; the chip makers in SMH sell to data centers everywhere.
baskets.watch: The same Texas policy headlines; bitcoin, which still drives part of their revenue; hyperscaler lease announcements.
baskets.source: IBKR themes Data Centers, Data Center Power; dossier 2026-11-03

members.why: Childress, Texas campus being converted to AI cloud
Denton, Texas among its AI hosting sites (CoreWeave tenant)
West Texas sites (Odessa, Barber Lake) aimed at HPC leases
Rockdale and Corsicana, Texas; Corsicana marketed for AI/HPC
Helios campus in West Texas, leased for AI compute
MARA: bitcoin miner with Texas sites and AI-power plans; moved here from Crypto stocks on 2026-11-09 after tracking this group (0.75) far more closely than crypto stocks (0.29) over 120 sessions

baskets.caution: RIOT's +11% runs against the rest of the group, which fell 10-19%, and is likely its own news; check before reading the basket.

baskets.name: Data-center power equipment
baskets.story: Suppliers of power, cooling and grid gear for AI data centers, national rather than Texas-specific. They fall when the market doubts the pace of the build-out, against industrials as a whole.
baskets.watch: Hyperscaler capex guidance (earnings), order and backlog updates, any federal or state limits on data-center grid hookups.

members.why: IBKR's top-ranked Data Center Power name: UPS, power distribution and cooling
Grid-to-chip power management; data-center orders up sharply
Gas turbines and grid equipment; $2.4B of data-center electrification orders in Q1
Fuel cells for on-site data-center power (Oracle's 2.45 GW deployment)
Power ICs for AI servers; about a third of revenue from AI and servers
nVent: liquid cooling and electrical connections; data centers about $1B in 2025, about a quarter of sales and rising
Powell: switchgear; one data-center order over $400M was about 43% of fiscal Q3 orders, commercial and other industrial 40% of backlog

baskets.name: Utility-scale solar
baskets.story: US utility-scale solar equipment makers, which gain if a Democratic Congress protects or extends clean-energy credits. Against XLU, the bet is on the policy, not on power demand.
baskets.watch: Senate control calls; statements on the clean-energy tax credits; tariff news on imported modules.

members.why: Largest US module maker; pure play on US utility-scale demand
Nextpower: solar trackers and balance-of-system for utility-scale plants
Electrical balance-of-system for utility-scale solar and storage
T1 Energy: US module maker (G1 Dallas), all sales from solar modules, $250M in Q2; reports Q3 on Nov 12
Canadian Solar: modules and storage, with roughly half of 2026 module shipments in the US (6.5-7.0 GW guided) and a Texas plant; only just clears the volume bar after being dropped at $19.5M on Nov 5

dropped.reason: average dollar volume $19.5M, under the $20M bar

baskets.name: Managed care
baskets.story: Health insurers, whose margins hang on Medicare Advantage rates and ACA and Medicaid funding, all set in Washington. A Democratic sweep changes those odds; the names split between Medicare Advantage-heavy (HUM, UNH) and ACA/Medicaid-heavy (CNC, ELV), so the basket is a test of the policy read, not a one-way bet.
baskets.watch: Medicare Advantage rate notices, ACA subsidy extension talk, company earnings (several report in early November).

members.why: Largest insurer; heavy Medicare Advantage exposure
The most Medicare Advantage-dependent large insurer
Commercial, Medicaid and ACA mix
The largest ACA marketplace and Medicaid insurer
Molina: Medicaid about 78% of Q3 premiums, Medicare 15%, Marketplace 6% after a deliberate retreat
Oscar: the ACA marketplace specialist, nearly all revenue from ACA plans, about 2.7M members; Q3 profit on Nov 5 with a Q4 loss implied by guidance

baskets.caution: CVS (-12%) and CNC (+13%) moved far apart, likely on their own news; check before reading the basket.

baskets.name: Memory and storage
baskets.story: Memory and storage makers whose prices ride AI data-center demand for DRAM, HBM, NAND and hard drives. Memory prices swing far harder than logic chips, so against SMH the spread isolates the memory cycle from chips as a whole.
baskets.watch: DRAM and NAND contract price reports, hyperscaler capex guidance, Micron's next earnings, HBM supply news from SK Hynix and Samsung.

members.why: DRAM about three quarters of sales and NAND the rest; HBM for AI accelerators. IBKR's top Memory Chips name
Sandisk: pure-play NAND flash and SSDs, spun out of Western Digital
Western Digital: hard drives for cloud storage since the Sandisk spin-off
Seagate: high-capacity hard drives for data centers
Silicon Motion: NAND flash controllers are its whole business; Q2 revenue $451M, up 127%; enterprise controllers 5-10% of 2026 revenue

baskets.name: Neoclouds
baskets.story: GPU cloud providers that rent AI compute to model labs and hyperscalers, built largely on debt and long leases. Against SMH, which sells them the chips, the spread reads the market's view of their financing and contract risk rather than AI demand itself.
baskets.watch: Debt raises and what they cost, new or renewed capacity contracts, GPU rental prices; for IREN and APLD, the same data-center siting politics as the Texas baskets.
baskets.source: IBKR theme Cloud Infrastructure (neocloud customers named by EQIX, SMCI, VRT, ANET)

members.why: CoreWeave: the largest listed neocloud, NVIDIA capacity leased to model labs and hyperscalers
Nebius: AI cloud in Europe and the US, with a large Microsoft capacity contract
Applied Digital: North Dakota AI campuses leased to CoreWeave
Converting its bitcoin sites to AI cloud; also in the Texas AI hosts basket
TeraWulf: HPC leases about 83% of Q3 revenue (Fluidstack, Anthropic); a landlord like APLD rather than a GPU renter
Cerebras: wafer-scale AI chips and its own inference cloud, cloud about 70% of Q2 reported revenue with OpenAI the driver; also a chip maker, so not a pure neocloud

baskets.name: AI networking and optics
baskets.story: Switches, optical transceivers, lasers and connectivity chips that link GPUs inside and between AI data centers. Against SMH, the spread shows whether networking is gaining or losing share of AI spending.
baskets.watch: Hyperscaler capex, earnings in the group (several report in early November), 800G and 1.6T optics orders, NVIDIA's own networking sales.
baskets.source: IBKR theme Cloud Infrastructure; member checks with IBKR

members.why: Arista: data-center switching for cloud titans and neoclouds
Ciena: optical transport between data centers
Coherent: optical transceivers and lasers for AI clusters
Lumentum: lasers and optical components for data-center links
Credo: active electrical cables and SerDes chips for AI racks
Astera Labs: PCIe and CXL connectivity chips for AI servers

baskets.caution: ANET (+5.7%) and COHR (+1.2%) rose while the other four fell 4-9%, likely on their own news in earnings season; check before reading the basket.

baskets.name: Nuclear fuel and new reactors
baskets.story: Uranium, enrichment and small-reactor names whose case rests on data-center demand and federal support for new nuclear. Unlike the operators in Texas power, most sell no power today, so they trade on policy and contracts. New nuclear has had support from both parties, so the election is a weaker read here.
baskets.watch: NRC licensing steps, DOE fuel and reactor awards, hyperscaler nuclear deals, uranium prices.

members.why: Aurora microreactors and fuel recycling; pre-revenue
NuScale: the only NRC-certified small modular reactor design
Centrus: the main US uranium enricher, building HALEU capacity
Naval reactors and nuclear components; supplier to commercial small reactors
Cameco: uranium mining and conversion, 49% of Westinghouse
Uranium Energy: US uranium miner and conversion developer, all FY2026 revenue ($37.3M) from uranium sales
Energy Fuels: uranium about 97% of Q3 revenue, but rare earths and the pending VAC deal are a growing part of the story
NANO Nuclear: KRONOS microreactor developer, essentially pre-revenue apart from small nuclear-transport sales; thin at about $24M a day

baskets.name: Quantum computing
baskets.story: Pure-play quantum computer makers, mostly pre-profit and heavily traded by retail. They move as one speculative high-beta group; against QQQ the spread is that appetite for speculation.
baskets.watch: Retail flows and options volume, equity raises, government funding news, technical milestones.

members.why: Trapped-ion systems; the largest pure play
Rigetti: superconducting systems sold through the major clouds
D-Wave: annealing and gate-model systems
Photonic systems; the smallest and thinnest of the four
Infleqtion: neutral-atom computers and quantum sensors, all revenue quantum, about 80% from US government customers; NASA sensing work was a main Q2 driver
Quantinuum: trapped-ion systems (Helios); Honeywell keeps about 48% of the vote; IPO June 4, so a six-month lockup would likely end around early December

baskets.name: Crypto stocks
baskets.story: An exchange, a retail broker, a stablecoin issuer and a bitcoin treasury company. Against IBIT, the spread strips out bitcoin's own move and leaves trading volumes, regulation and MSTR's premium to its holdings.
baskets.watch: Crypto market-structure and stablecoin rules under the new Congress, SEC posture, exchange volumes, MSTR's premium to its bitcoin.

members.why: Coinbase: the largest US crypto exchange; trading is over half of revenue
Robinhood: retail broker with about 18% of revenue from crypto
Strategy: holds bitcoin as its main asset
Circle: issues USDC and earns interest on the reserves, so it is also rate-sensitive
BitMine: ether treasury, about 95% of $14.5B in assets (6.06M ETH on Nov 1). IBIT is bitcoin, so the spread carries ether against bitcoin
Bullish: institutional crypto exchange for spot, derivatives and options; all revenue from digital-asset trading

baskets.name: Space
baskets.story: Launch, satellite and lunar companies that live on NASA and defense contracts plus private funding. Against XLI, the spread is the speculative and government-contract premium on top of industrials.
baskets.watch: NASA and Space Force budget lines in the new Congress, launch results, contract awards, equity raises.

members.why: Rocket Lab: Electron launches, spacecraft and the coming Neutron rocket
AST SpaceMobile: satellites that connect directly to ordinary phones
Intuitive Machines: NASA lunar landers and services
Planet Labs: daily Earth imaging satellites for government and business
Redwire: space infrastructure and components for NASA missions
Voyager: Starlab commercial station and space infrastructure; nearly three quarters of capex and innovation spending on space; Q3 revenue $89M, up 124%
Firefly: Blue Ghost lunar landers and Alpha rockets, spacecraft 83.5% of Q2 revenue; reports Q3 on Nov 10 after the close
SpaceX: launch and Starlink, connectivity about 61% of 2025 revenue; IPO June 2026 and by far the largest name in the group

baskets.name: Defense primes
baskets.story: The large US defense contractors, paid almost entirely from the federal budget. A Democratic Congress changes the odds on defense spending growth; against XLI the spread is that budget read.
baskets.watch: Defense appropriations and any continuing resolution, the next budget request, large program awards, Ukraine and Middle East aid votes.
baskets.source: IBKR theme Space Exploration (LMT, NOC); member checks with IBKR

members.why: Lockheed Martin: F-35, missiles and the Orion spacecraft
Northrop Grumman: B-21 bomber, Sentinel ICBM and space systems
General Dynamics: submarines, combat vehicles and Gulfstream jets
RTX: Raytheon missiles and Pratt & Whitney engines
L3Harris: defense electronics, communications and rocket motors
Huntington Ingalls: Navy shipbuilder, shipbuilding about 80% of Q3 revenue ($2.8B of $3.5B) and the rest Mission Technologies

baskets.name: Life science tools
baskets.story: Makers of lab instruments, reagents and bioprocessing supplies sold to drug makers, biotechs and academic labs. Demand hangs on NIH and university funding, biotech financing and China, and a Democratic Congress is usually read as kinder to NIH budgets. Against XLV, the spread separates the tools business from insurers and drug makers.
baskets.watch: NIH budget and grant flow in appropriations, biotech funding and IPOs, China demand and tariffs, earnings in the group (several report in early November).

members.why: Thermo Fisher: the largest tools maker, from instruments to reagents and drug manufacturing services
Danaher: bioprocessing, Beckman Coulter, SCIEX and Abcam
Agilent: chromatography, mass spectrometry and lab consumables
Waters: liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry, now with BD's biosciences business
Illumina: genomic sequencers and their consumables; IBKR's top Life Science Tools name
Bio-Techne: research proteins, antibodies and analytical instruments
Revvity: life-science instruments, reagents and lab software
10x Genomics: single-cell and spatial biology instruments and reagents for research labs; smaller and more exposed to academic funding than the rest of the group

baskets.caution: ILMN (-4.7%) and RVTY (-2.5%) fell while the other five rose, possibly on their own news in earnings season; check before reading the basket.

baskets.name: Cybersecurity
baskets.story: Security software vendors, where budgets tend to hold up better than other IT spending and AI adds new attack surfaces. Against IGV, the spread shows security against software broadly.
baskets.watch: Earnings and billings guidance across the group, large breaches, platform consolidation deals, and whether AI agents are read as a threat to software or a new thing to secure.

members.why: Palo Alto Networks: pure-play security platform; bought CyberArk for identity
CrowdStrike: endpoint and cloud security on its Falcon platform
Fortinet: firewalls and secure networking, with custom chips
Zscaler: cloud zero-trust access
Okta: identity and access management; joined the S&P 500 on Nov 4
SentinelOne: AI-driven endpoint and cloud detection
Rubrik: data security and ransomware recovery

baskets.caution: PANW and CRWD are also large IGV holdings, so the spread understates the group's move. CHKP rose while the others fell 5-11% today; check for its own news.

baskets.name: Hyperscalers
baskets.story: The companies paying for the AI buildout. When money leaves chip suppliers it can move here, because lower capex helps their free cash flow, or it can leave too if AI demand itself is doubted. Against QQQ, which they dominate.
baskets.watch: Capex guidance, free cash flow (reported negative at several of them), debt issuance for data centers, and whether they hold up when SMH sells off.
baskets.source: Dossier 2026-11-05; Reuters on rotation from chips into hyperscalers

members.why: Microsoft: Azure and OpenAI exposure
Alphabet: Google Cloud, TPUs and search
Amazon: AWS and custom chips
Meta: AI capex without a cloud business to sell it through
Oracle: debt-funded AI cloud buildout, the group's most levered name

baskets.caution: All five are in or near QQQ's largest holdings, except ORCL, which isn't in it, so the spread is narrow and ORCL often drives it.

baskets.name: Chip equipment
baskets.story: Makers of the tools that build chips. Their orders follow fab spending, including memory, so they often lead when capex expectations change. Against SMH to separate tools from chip designers.
baskets.watch: Memory capex, TSMC capex guidance, China export rules, and earnings from AMAT and others in the group.

members.why: Applied Materials: broadest tool maker
Lam Research: etch and deposition, with heavy memory exposure; announced a $25B buyback tonight
KLA: inspection and process control
ASML: lithography, the only maker of EUV tools
Teradyne: chip testing, tied to AI accelerators; also a robotics business
Onto Innovation: process control and inspection for advanced nodes and packaging; all revenue is chip equipment
MKS: vacuum, plasma and RF subsystems inside chip tools, semiconductors over 40% of revenue and the rest electronics and specialty

baskets.caution: AMAT, LRCX, KLAC and ASML are also large SMH holdings, so the spread understates the group's move.

baskets.name: Robotics and automation
baskets.story: Warehouse robots, factory automation, machine vision and lidar: the listed names closest to physical AI. Against XLI, the spread shows whether the theme is trading on its own.
baskets.watch: Earnings and order commentary, factory capex and PMIs, humanoid robot news, NVIDIA's physical AI announcements.

members.why: Symbotic: warehouse robots, over 90% of revenue, with Walmart as its main customer
Rockwell Automation: factory automation and mobile robots
Cognex: machine vision for factories and logistics
Ouster: lidar sensors; robotics is its second-largest market
Hesai (China ADR): lidar, robotics about 23% of Q2 units and nearly tripling; left out at $18M a day on Nov 5 and now only just clears
Novanta: motion control and precision robotic components; robotics and automation about 20% of sales, up 13.5% in Q2; the rest is mostly medical

baskets.caution: ROK fell 14% today after reporting before the open, more than the group. HSAI was left out: about $18M a day in volume. SYM, at about $38M a day, is the next thinnest.

baskets.name: Copper miners
baskets.story: Copper producers, tied to electrification, data-center demand and China. They trade with the metal and swing harder than broad materials.
baskets.watch: Copper price, China stimulus and demand data, US tariff news, mine disruptions such as Grasberg.

members.why: Freeport-McMoRan: the largest US copper producer; each $0.10 per pound moves annual EBITDA about $400M
Southern Copper: copper about 70% of revenue
Teck Resources: copper and zinc after selling its coal business
Hudbay Minerals: copper and gold mines in the Americas
Ero Copper: Brazilian mines, copper about 73% of Q3 revenue and gold the rest, with stockpile gold flattering the quarter
Trekor Metals (renamed from Taseko in June): Gibraltar and Florence copper mines, 36M lb of copper in Q2; revenue share not stated in the sources

baskets.caution: FCX is also a large XLB holding, and these names can trade with gold as well as copper.

baskets.name: Airlines, cruises and bookings
baskets.story: Travel demand with a large oil exposure. Fuel is a top cost for airlines and cruise lines, so this group is a read on the Iran and Hormuz story as well as the consumer. Against XLY, which is dominated by Amazon and Tesla.
baskets.watch: Oil and Hormuz headlines, airline capacity and fares, consumer confidence, jobs data.

members.why: Delta: premium-heavy airline
United: long-haul and international airline
Royal Caribbean: largest cruise operator by value
Carnival: higher debt, more leverage to fuel
Norwegian: smallest and most levered of the cruise three
Booking: online travel, no fuel bill

baskets.caution: BKNG and ABNB have no fuel exposure, so they soften the oil read.

baskets.name: Drones and defense tech
baskets.story: Smaller defense names built on unmanned systems, closer to the Iran war and drone warfare than the primes are. They carry far more retail and momentum money than LMT or NOC.
baskets.watch: Pentagon drone programs and budget talk under a Democratic Congress, Iran news, contract awards, share sales.
baskets.source: IBKR theme Robotics (AVAV); member checks with IBKR

members.why: AeroVironment: unmanned aircraft and loitering munitions
Kratos: target and combat drones, hypersonics
Red Cat: small military drones
Ondas: drone and autonomous systems
Unusual Machines: US drone motors and components, nearly all revenue; Q3 revenue $13.9M, up 551%
AEVEX: military drones and loitering munitions, Tactical Systems about 88% of quarterly revenue; IPO April 2026, Madison Dearborn holds 79% of the vote, only just clears the volume bar

baskets.caution: RCAT and ONDS fell 14-15% today and are thin, speculative names; RCAT is the thinnest, at about $44M a day.

baskets.name: Refiners
baskets.story: US refiners earn the gap between crude and fuel, not the price of oil. XLE is mostly producers, so the spread isolates the crack: diesel and gasoline margins hit records in Q3 2026 on Middle East and Ukraine supply losses.
baskets.watch: Weekly 3-2-1 and diesel crack spreads, EIA refinery utilization and distillate stocks, Hormuz and Russian product headlines, whether the CVR-Marathon refinery sale closes around year-end, small refinery exemption rulings for CVI, DK and PARR.
baskets.source: No IBKR refining theme exists (searched refining, refiner, petroleum); Q3 2026 company releases, Oct 22 to Nov 6, 2026

members.why: Marathon Petroleum: Refining & Marketing about 85% of Q3 2026 segment EBITDA ($9.9B of $11.7B), the rest mostly MPLX midstream; selling St. Paul Park and Mandan to CVI (MPC release, Nov 2026)
Valero: refining about 93% of Q3 2026 segment operating income ($8.78B of $9.41B), plus renewable diesel and ethanol (Valero 8-K, Oct 22, 2026)
Phillips 66: refining about 85% of Q3 2026 adjusted segment income, but about a third in Q3 2025, with midstream and CPChem the rest (Phillips 66 results, Oct 28, 2026)
PBF Energy: nearly pure refiner, about 924,000 bpd of throughput across four regions, with a renewable diesel joint venture; refining share not itemized (PBF 8-K, Oct 30, 2026)
HF Sinclair: refining about 87% of Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA ($2.58B of $2.98B), plus lubricants, renewables and midstream (HF Sinclair release, Oct 28, 2026)
Delek US: refining about 97% of Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA ($1.24B of $1.28B), with Delek Logistics the rest (Delek release, Nov 6, 2026)

CVR Energy: petroleum about 97% of Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA ($565M of $582M), nitrogen fertilizer the rest; buying two Marathon refineries for $4.2B, nearly doubling capacity; it is the buyer, so no price pin (CVR release, Nov 3, 2026)
Par Pacific: refining about 61% of Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA ($396M of $646M, per the call, not checked against the release), plus logistics and retail in Hawaii and the Rockies (Q3 call, Nov 3, 2026)

baskets.name: Seat-based software
baskets.story: Software priced per user, where the fear is that AI agents do the work of paid seats and customers buy fewer. monday.com fell 21% in February after flagging agents as a threat, and Atlassian's call brought up seat compression. Against IGV, the spread is that fear, without the infrastructure and security names.
baskets.watch: Net revenue retention and seat counts in earnings, how fast seats-plus-credits pricing spreads, Workday and Silver Lake headlines, Salesforce's next results (early December), any further take-private of a seat-based name.
baskets.source: IBKR theme SaaS (evidence pulled 2026-11-09); company results, Sep to Nov 2026

members.why: Salesforce: per-user CRM licenses at the core; subscription about 95% of sales, with Agentforce sold on seats, credits and outcomes (IBKR SaaS, Nov 2026)
ServiceNow: priced per fulfiller, subscription virtually all revenue; about half of new business now on a seat-plus-consumption hybrid (IBKR SaaS, Nov 2026)

Workday: priced on customer headcount, subscription 93% of revenue. Silver Lake talks reported Aug 13 and still live Sep 17; no signed deal or terms found, so not pinned, status since unconfirmed (IBKR SaaS, Nov 2026; Reuters, Aug 13, 2026)

Adobe: per-user Creative Cloud; Creative and Marketing Professionals subscriptions 69% of Q3 FY26 revenue ($4.65B of $6.76B). The fear is more generative AI replacing creative work than agents cutting seats (Adobe release, Sep 2026)
Atlassian: Jira and Confluence seat subscriptions; Cloud 73% of Q1 FY27 revenue ($1.30B of $1.77B), and management has used the phrase seat compression (Atlassian release, Nov 5, 2026; IBKR SaaS)
HubSpot: priced on Core Seats with bundled AI credits; subscription 98% of revenue; Q4 guide below Q3 on weaker demand (HubSpot Q3 release, Nov 2026; IBKR SaaS)
monday.com: seat plans, with seats-plus-credits for customers joining after May 6, 2026; Q3 revenue $377.5M, up 19%, reported today (monday.com release, Nov 9, 2026)
Asana: revenue entirely from tiered, seat-based subscriptions, about $800M a year; 96% net retention. The purest seat name here (IBKR SaaS, Nov 2026)

baskets.name: Rare earths and critical minerals
baskets.story: Producers of minerals China dominates, where Washington now buys stakes, sets price floors and stockpiles. MP has a 15% federal stake and an NdPr floor of $110/kg; USA Rare Earth has a pending $1.6B Commerce deal; antimony and tungsten are under Chinese export limits. Against XLB, the spread is that policy bid, which has faded quickly after past deals.
baskets.watch: The US-China truce on rare earth exports, reported to expire in November 2026; any new federal stake, floor or Defense Logistics Agency order; NdPr price against the $110/kg floor; USA Rare Earth Q3 results after the close today, 4:30 PM ET call; US Antimony Q3 results (Nov 10 or 16, dates conflict).
baskets.source: IBKR themes Rare Earth Elements, Critical Minerals; S&P Global, Oct 20, 2026; company releases

members.why: MP Materials: essentially 100% rare earths; Q3 2026 revenue $147.6M including $8.1M of federal price-protection income (MP release, Nov 5, 2026; IBKR Rare Earth Elements)
USA Rare Earth: 100% of revenue from Less Common Metals, buying Serra Verde, $1.6B Commerce funding pending; Q3 results after the close today (IBKR Rare Earth Elements, Nov 2026; company notice)
US Antimony: antimony about 75% of Q2 2026 revenue ($5.9M of $7.9M), zeolite the rest; $245M sole-source Defense Logistics Agency contract (10-Q, Aug 2026). At the volume bar, $21M a day

Almonty: tungsten miner, Q1 2026 revenue $25.4M on record tungsten prices; Korea's Sangdong mine started processing July 1, 2026; China controls tungsten exports; exact split not found (Almonty Q1 report; company release, Jul 1, 2026)
Albemarle: lithium-led Energy Storage about 72% of Q3 2026 sales ($1.12B of $1.55B); IBKR's top Critical Minerals name, but no federal stake or floor (Albemarle 8-K, Nov 2026)

baskets.watch: VLCC rates on the Middle East to China route, Hormuz transit counts and the US-Iran deal terms, DHT and Frontline Q4 booking updates, Hafnia's stake in TORM.
baskets.source: IBKR theme Shipping Routes (FRO, STNG, DHT, TNK, TRMD); Q2 and Q3 2026 company results

DHT Holdings: VLCC-only fleet, Q3 2026 spot VLCCs earned about $167,100 a day (DHT update, Oct 12, 2026)
International Seaways: tankers are the whole business, crude and product; Q3 2026 VLCC spot averaged about $154,600 a day (INSW Q3 release, Nov 2026)
Teekay Tankers: Suezmax and Aframax tankers are the whole business; Q3 Suezmax bookings about $104,800 a day at late July, 44% booked (Teekay 6-K, Jul 2026)
Nordic American: 17 Suezmaxes, the whole business; about 75% of Q3 days booked near $54,000 a day (NAT Q2 report, Aug 2026)

TORM (NASDAQ line): product tankers only, 95 vessels; no merger terms found, so not pinned, but Hafnia is at about 19.85% after its latest purchase and wants a combination (TORM Q3 release; Hafnia notice, Sep 23, 2026)
